title: Allow isolating containers within network
body:
### Feature request description

Isolating containers within a network from each other, similarly to how `isolate=true` works.

### Suggest potential solution

A container option that enables isolation, possibly combined with a network option that applies the option to all members, with the ability to override it per container.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Using separate networks. Too much administrative overhead for dozens of single container networks.

### Additional context

This is useful for reverse proxy setups, where one, non isolated container can connect to a number of other, isolated containers, which can not connect to each other.

I'm not sure how this will differ between rootful and rootless environments. Related issue:
https://github.com/containers/netavark/issues/1009

I'm currently using this script (boilerplate not included) in `ExecStartPost` in a rootful environment with great success:
```py
container_id = args.container

# For pods, the network is attached to the infra container.
if args.pod:
	pod = run(f'podman pod inspect {container_id}', True)
	container_id = pod[0]['InfraContainerID']

container = run(f'podman container inspect {container_id}', True)
container = container[0]
container_id = container['Id']

network = run(f'podman network inspect {args.network}', True)
network = network[0]

if not container_id in network['containers']:
	sys.exit("Container is not part of network")

bridge_links = run(f'bridge -json link show', True)
bridge_links = { link['ifindex']: link for link in bridge_links }

container_pid = container['State']['Pid']

for iface in network['containers'][container_id]['interfaces']:
	with open(f'/proc/{container_pid}/root/sys/class/net/{iface}/iflink') as f:
		interface_index = int(f.read().strip())
		interface_name = bridge_links[interface_index]['ifname']
		run(f'bridge link set dev {interface_name} isolated on')

```
